senses.def: a piece of furniture or a space in a wall with doors and shelves, used for storing things
examples: The plates are in the cupboard above the sink.
We keep cleaning supplies in the cupboard under the stairs.

note: Pronounced /ˈkʌbərd/: the p is silent. Americans usually say "cabinet" in kitchens and "closet" for clothes.

senses.def: a medicine or treatment that makes an illness go away
examples: Scientists are still searching for a cure for Alzheimer's.
There is no cure for the common cold.

senses.def: something that solves a problem
examples: Lower taxes are not a cure for every economic problem.

senses.def: to make a person or animal healthy again, or to end an illness or problem
examples: The treatment cured her of the infection in two weeks.
Nothing will cure his habit of arriving late.

note: "Cure" means to fully heal; "treat" means to give medical care, which may or may not cure.

senses.def: a strong wish to know or learn about something
examples: Out of curiosity, I opened the box to see what was inside.
Children are full of natural curiosity about the world.

senses.def: an unusual and interesting object or person
examples: The old shop was full of curiosities from around the world.

note: "Curiosity killed the cat" warns that being too curious can get you into trouble.

senses.def: wanting to know or learn about something
examples: I'm curious to know how the story ends.
The kids were curious about the strange noise in the attic.

senses.def: strange and unusual
examples: There was a curious smell coming from the basement.

note: "Just curious" is a polite way to show you're asking out of interest, not suspicion.

senses.def: having curls or a curved shape
examples: She has long curly hair that she usually ties back.
The puppy has a short curly tail.

note: Opposite: straight hair. "Curly brackets" are { }.

senses.def: the system of money used in a particular country
examples: The euro is the official currency of 20 European countries.
You can exchange foreign currency at the airport.

senses.def: the state of being generally accepted or used
examples: The idea gained currency among economists in the 1980s.

note: "Gain currency" = become widely accepted (used for ideas and words).

senses.def: happening or existing now
examples: What's your current address?
The current situation is better than it was a year ago.

senses.def: a movement of water or air in a particular direction
examples: The current was too strong for the swimmers.
Warm ocean currents keep the coast mild in winter.

senses.def: a flow of electricity through a wire
examples: Turn off the current before you touch the wires.

note: Don't confuse with "currant" (a small dried fruit), which sounds the same.

senses.def: at the present time
examples: She's currently working on her second novel.
The museum is currently closed for renovation.

note: Trap for Turkish speakers: "actually" does NOT mean "currently" (aktüel). Use "currently" for "şu anda".

senses.def: the subjects included in a course of study or taught in a school
examples: Coding has been added to the elementary school curriculum.
The university is reviewing its curriculum for first-year students.

note: Plural: curricula or curriculums. A CV (curriculum vitae) is usually called a "résumé" in the US.

senses.def: a piece of cloth hung to cover a window or divide a space
examples: Could you close the curtains? The sun is in my eyes.
She pulled back the shower curtain.

senses.def: the large cloth in front of a theater stage
examples: The audience clapped as the curtain came down.

note: Americans also say "drapes" for heavy curtains. "Curtain call" = when actors come back to bow.

senses.def: a line or surface that bends smoothly, or a bend in a road
examples: Slow down: there's a sharp curve ahead.
The graph shows a steady upward curve in sales.

senses.def: to bend or move in a smooth round line
examples: The path curves gently down to the beach.
The ball curved into the top corner of the net.

note: "A steep learning curve" = something that takes a lot of effort to learn quickly.

senses.def: having a round, bent shape rather than a straight one
examples: The bridge has a beautiful curved design.
A parrot uses its strong curved beak to crack nuts.

note: Opposite: straight.

senses.def: the legal right to care for a child, especially after parents separate
examples: After the divorce, the mother was given custody of the children.
They share joint custody of their son.

senses.def: the state of being held by the police, usually before a trial
examples: The suspect is now in police custody.
Two men were taken into custody after the robbery.

note: In the US, a "custodian" is also a building janitor.

senses.def: a traditional way of doing something in a society or group
examples: In Japan, it is the custom to take off your shoes indoors.
Giving gifts at New Year is an old local custom.

senses.def: made specially for a particular customer
examples: They ordered custom furniture for the new house.

note: "Customs" (plural) is the place at a border where bags are checked: "go through customs".

senses.def: a person or organization that buys goods or services from a business
examples: The store gives regular customers a 10% discount.
Call customer service if your package doesn't arrive.

note: "Client" is used for professional services (lawyers, agencies); "customer" for shops and companies.

senses.def: to divide, open, or shape something with a knife, scissors, or other sharp tool
examples: Cut the onions into small pieces.
I cut my finger while opening the package.

senses.def: to reduce the amount, size, or number of something
examples: The company plans to cut 2,000 jobs this year.
Try to cut down on sugar.

senses.def: a wound made by something sharp
examples: He had a deep cut on his hand from the broken glass.

senses.def: a reduction in amount or size
examples: Teachers protested against the budget cuts.

note: Irregular verb: cut – cut – cut. "Cut it out!" (informal) = stop doing that.

senses.def: pretty and attractive, especially in a small or childlike way
examples: Look at that cute little puppy!
The baby looks so cute in that hat.

senses.def: (informal) sexually attractive
examples: She thinks the new guy at work is really cute.

senses.def: trying too hard to be clever, in an annoying way
examples: Don't get cute with me; just answer the question.

senses.def: (British) an article or picture cut from a newspaper or magazine
examples: Her mother kept a folder of newspaper cuttings about her career.

senses.def: a piece cut from a plant to grow a new plant
examples: I took a cutting from my neighbor's rose bush and planted it.

senses.def: unkind and meant to hurt someone's feelings, or (of wind) very cold
examples: He made a cutting remark about her weight.
A cutting wind blew off the lake.

note: Americans say "newspaper clipping" rather than "cutting". "Cutting-edge" = the most advanced.

senses.def: a series of events that repeat in the same order
examples: The program aims to break the cycle of poverty.
The washing machine takes an hour to finish one cycle.

senses.def: a bicycle or motorcycle
examples: The city has built new cycle lanes downtown.

senses.def: to ride a bicycle
examples: She cycles to work every day, even in winter.

note: In everyday American English, people usually say "bike" and "ride a bike" rather than "cycle".

senses.tr: kinik, şüpheci, her şeye kötü gözle bakan
senses.def: believing that people usually act only for selfish reasons, not honest or good ones
examples: Many voters have become cynical about politicians' promises.
Years of working in sales made him cynical.

senses.def: caring only about your own advantage, without regard for others
examples: The ad campaign was a cynical attempt to make money from a tragedy.

senses.def: (informal) father
examples: My dad taught me how to ride a bike.
Dad, can you pick me up after practice?

note: Write "Dad" with a capital letter when used as a name. A "dad joke" is a corny, predictable joke.

senses.def: happening, done, or produced every day
examples: Exercise should be part of your daily routine.
The museum gets about 5,000 daily visitors.

senses.def: every day
examples: Take the medicine twice daily with food.
The newspaper is published daily.

senses.def: a newspaper published every day
examples: The story was on the front page of every national daily.

senses.def: milk, cheese, butter, and other foods made from milk
examples: She's allergic to dairy, so she drinks oat milk.
Try to eat less meat and dairy.

senses.def: made from milk, or connected with producing milk
examples: Dairy products are a good source of calcium.
He grew up on a dairy farm in Wisconsin.

note: Don't confuse "dairy" /ˈderi/ with "diary" /ˈdaɪəri/ (a daily journal).

senses.def: a wall built across a river to hold back water, often to make a lake or produce electricity
examples: The Hoover Dam supplies electricity to millions of people.
Heavy rain caused the old dam to burst.

senses.def: to build a dam across a river
examples: The river was dammed in the 1960s to create a reservoir.

note: Don't confuse with "damn" (a swear word), which sounds the same.

senses.def: physical harm that makes something less useful, valuable, or attractive
examples: The storm caused serious damage to homes along the coast.
Smoking can cause permanent damage to your lungs.

senses.def: to harm something physically, or to have a bad effect on something
examples: Several cars were damaged in the flood.
The scandal damaged the company's reputation.

senses.def: money that a court orders someone to pay for causing harm or loss
examples: She was awarded $2 million in damages.

note: "Damage" (harm) is uncountable: "a lot of damage", not "damages". "Damages" means money paid by court order.

senses.def: causing harm or having a bad effect
examples: The leaked emails were deeply damaging to her campaign.
Too much sun can be damaging to your skin.

senses.def: to move your body to music
examples: We danced all night at their wedding.
Do you want to dance?

senses.def: a set of movements done to music, or an occasion when people dance
examples: The tango is a dance from Argentina.
Are you going to the school dance on Friday?

senses.def: a person who dances, especially as a job
examples: She trained as a ballet dancer in New York.
I'm not a very good dancer, so I'll just watch.

note: In Turkish "dansöz" means a belly dancer; in English that is "belly dancer". "Dancer" is general.

senses.def: the activity of moving your body to music
examples: Let's go dancing on Saturday night.
She takes dancing lessons twice a week.

senses.def: the possibility of being hurt, killed, or harmed
examples: The sign warned of danger from falling rocks.
Doctors say the patient is now out of danger.

senses.def: something or someone that may cause harm, or the risk that something bad will happen
examples: Icy roads are a real danger to drivers.
There's a danger that prices will rise again.

senses.def: likely to cause injury, harm, or damage
examples: It's dangerous to text while driving.
Police say the escaped prisoner is armed and dangerous.

senses.def: to be brave enough to do something
examples: Nobody dared to tell the boss about the mistake.
I didn't dare look down from the top of the tower.

senses.tr: (birine bir şey yapması için) meydan okumak
senses.def: to challenge someone to do something dangerous or difficult
examples: His friends dared him to jump into the freezing lake.

senses.def: a challenge to do something risky
examples: She ate the hot pepper on a dare.

note: "How dare you!" expresses anger. "Don't you dare!" is a strong warning. "Dare" can be followed by an infinitive with or without "to".

senses.def: with little or no light
examples: It gets dark around five o'clock in winter.
The hallway was too dark to see anything.

senses.def: close to black in color, or (of hair, eyes, skin) brown or black
examples: He wore a dark blue suit to the interview.
She has dark hair and green eyes.

senses.def: sad, unpleasant, or evil
examples: The film has a much darker ending than the book.

senses.def: the lack of light, especially at night
examples: Many kids are afraid of the dark.
Be home before dark.

note: "Keep someone in the dark" = not tell them what is happening.

senses.def: the state of having no light
examples: The power went out and the whole street was plunged into darkness.
We drove home in darkness after the concert.

senses.def: evil or sadness
examples: The novel explores the darkness inside ordinary people.

note: "Under cover of darkness" = hidden by the night.

senses.def: facts or information, especially when collected and studied to learn something or make decisions
examples: The data shows a sharp rise in housing prices.
Researchers collected data from over 10,000 patients.

senses.def: information stored or used by a computer, or mobile internet usage
examples: I've used up all my data for this month.
Hackers stole personal data from millions of users.

note: In American English, "data" is usually treated as uncountable: "the data is". "The data are" is more formal/academic.

senses.def: an organized collection of information stored on a computer that can be searched easily
examples: The police checked his fingerprints against a national database.
All customer orders are stored in a central database.

senses.def: a particular day of the month or year
examples: What's the date today?
Please write the date at the top of the form.

senses.def: a romantic meeting, or a person you go out with romantically
examples: They went on their first date to a little Italian restaurant.
Who's your date for the wedding?

senses.def: to have a romantic relationship with someone
examples: They dated for three years before getting married.

senses.tr: tarih atmak; (yaşını) tarihlendirmek; (from ile) -den kalma olmak
senses.def: to write the date on something, or to say or show how old something is
examples: The letter was dated May 3, 1945.
This church dates from the 12th century.

note: US date format is month/day/year: 3/5/2026 = March 5. "Date" is also the sweet fruit (hurma).

senses.def: a person's female child
examples: They have two sons and a daughter.
My daughter just started kindergarten.

note: The "gh" is silent: /ˈdɔːtər/. A "daughter-in-law" is your son's wife (gelin).

senses.def: the time of day when light first appears
examples: We left at dawn to avoid the traffic.
The fishermen work from dawn until dusk.

senses.def: the beginning of a period of time or of something new
examples: The invention of the printing press marked the dawn of a new age.

senses.def: if something dawns on you, you realize it for the first time
examples: It suddenly dawned on me that I had left my passport at home.

note: "It dawned on me" = I suddenly realized. Opposite of dawn: dusk.

senses.def: a period of 24 hours
examples: The store is open seven days a week.
I'll call you in a few days.

senses.def: the time when it is light outside, between sunrise and sunset
examples: He works during the day and studies at night.

senses.def: a particular period in history or in someone's life
examples: In my grandfather's day, nobody had a phone at home.
These days, almost everyone works online.

note: "Call it a day" = stop working for now. "The other day" = a few days ago.

senses.def: no longer alive
examples: Two people were found dead in the burned house.
My grandparents have been dead for years.

senses.def: not working because of no power, or very quiet with no activity
examples: My phone is dead; can I borrow your charger?
This town is completely dead after 9 p.m.

senses.def: (informal) completely or exactly
examples: I'm dead serious about quitting my job.
The hotel is dead ahead, at the end of the street.

note: "Dead" is the adjective, "die" the verb, "death" the noun. Don't say "He is died"; say "He is dead" or "He died".

senses.def: a time or date by which something must be finished
examples: The deadline for applications is March 1.
I'm working late tonight to meet a deadline.

senses.def: causing or likely to cause death
examples: It was the deadliest earthquake in the country's history.
Some mushrooms in these woods are deadly.

senses.def: extremely serious or accurate, or (informal) very boring
examples: She's a deadly accurate shooter.
He said it in deadly earnest.

note: "Deadly" is an adjective despite the -ly ending. "Fatal" describes something that actually killed; "deadly" can mean able to kill.

senses.def: an agreement, especially in business, about buying, selling, or doing something
examples: The two companies signed a $3 billion deal.
I got a great deal on this laptop.

senses.def: a large amount
examples: She spends a great deal of time helping others.

senses.tr: (with ile) ilgilenmek, başa çıkmak, ele almak
senses.def: to take action to solve a problem or handle a situation or person
examples: The manager will deal with your complaint.
I can't deal with this right now.

senses.def: to give out playing cards, or to buy and sell drugs or goods
examples: It's your turn to deal the cards.
He was arrested for dealing drugs.

note: Irregular verb: deal – dealt – dealt. "No big deal" = not important.

senses.def: a person or business that buys and sells a particular product
examples: We bought the car from a dealer in New Jersey.
She's an art dealer with a gallery in Chicago.

senses.def: a person who sells illegal drugs
examples: Police arrested three drug dealers near the park.

senses.def: used at the start of a letter or email before the person's name
examples: Dear Ms. Lopez, thank you for your application.
She started the email with "Dear team".

senses.def: loved by someone, or very important to them
examples: She's a dear friend of mine.
This house is very dear to me.

senses.def: used to show surprise, worry, or disappointment
examples: Oh dear, I've forgotten my wallet again.
Dear me, look at the time!

senses.def: used to speak to someone you love or are being kind to
examples: Thank you, dear, that's very kind.

note: "Pay dearly" = suffer a lot because of a mistake. In British English, "dear" can mean expensive.

senses.def: the end of someone's life, or the fact of dying
examples: The cause of death is still unknown.
His father's death hit him very hard.

senses.def: the end of something
examples: Online shopping has meant the death of many small bookstores.

note: "To death" adds emphasis: bored to death, scared to death. "Death toll" = number of people killed.

senses.def: a formal discussion in which people with different opinions argue, often followed by a vote
examples: The two candidates will face each other in a televised debate.
There is a heated debate over gun control.

senses.def: to discuss something formally, or to think carefully before deciding
examples: Congress is debating a new immigration bill.
I debated whether to call her or not.

note: "Debate" is used without "about" as a verb: "debate the issue", not "debate about the issue".

senses.def: broken pieces of something left after it has been destroyed
examples: Rescue workers searched through the debris after the earthquake.
The storm left debris scattered across the highway.

note: Pronounced /dəˈbriː/: the s is silent. Uncountable: "a lot of debris".

senses.def: money that someone owes, or the state of owing money
examples: Many students graduate with huge debts.
He's been in debt since he lost his job.

senses.def: a feeling that you should be grateful to someone for their help
examples: I owe you a debt of gratitude for all your support.

note: The b is silent: /det/. "In debt" = owing money.
